name: Hughes Station
headline: The Brighton Housing Authority is resyndicating and renovating Hughes Station, an existing 120-unit tax credit property for households at 30% to 60% AMI at 233 North Main Street in downtown Brighton, using a 2023-cycle federal 4% credit and CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: A housing authority preservation deal that recycles a property bought from a nonprofit in 2017: CHFA bonds, a CHFA HUD Risk Share loan, Capital Magnet Fund money, a $3.6M state grant, county CDBG and a seller carryback loan fund an $11M renovation while deepening affordability to an average of about 48% AMI.

status.label: Financing committed in 2024; renovation underway in 2025; resident celebration held July 2026
status.detail: CHFA reported providing the construction-to-permanent loan in February 2025, and the housing authority said construction would run through 2025 and 2026. The housing authority's project site invited residents to a celebration on 2026-07-25 for 'the families who now call Hughes Station home'; no public record found confirms final completion or the issue of 8609 forms (the deal is still on CHFA's 4% award report, which excludes developments with 8609s issued).

next_step: Watch Brighton Housing Authority board packets for a construction completion report and CHFA's 4% Completed Developments Report for 8609 issuance.

key_numbers.meaning: 18 one-, 60 two- and 42 three-bedroom units; 18 at 30%, 18 at 40%, 51 at 50% and 33 at 60% AMI (average about 48% AMI).
Cycle year 2023 on CHFA's report (the housing authority says the reservation came in June 2024); expected to raise about $11.0M of equity from National Equity Fund.
CHFA is the issuer per the award report; CHFA's February 2025 newsletter cites $16,340,000 of private activity bonds.
Includes an $11M transfer price from the housing authority to the new partnership and about $11.2M of construction (2024 staff memo; subject to change).

background.text: The Brighton Housing Authority took over Hughes Station from Almost Home, Inc., a homeless-services nonprofit that built and ran it, in a transaction reported at $10 million; the authority assumed the property's loans and Almost Home expected to net less than $1 million. The authority dates the purchase to 2017; the news report ran in January 2018.
Since 2021 the authority worked on a refinancing plan for significant deferred maintenance; CHFA issued conditional commitment letters on 2022-01-11 and final commitment letters on 2024-09-04.

At a 2024-09-12 special meeting the housing authority board approved Resolution 24-09-03 to use authority investment funds for the CHFA commitment fees, and the 2024-10-03 board agenda carried Resolution 24-10-01 to form the partnership, convey the property and approve the rehab financing.
The rehab deepens affordability: the property's original credits capped rents for households under 60% AMI, while the new mix puts 87 of 120 units at 50% AMI or below (computed from the CHFA mix).
The housing authority, a HUD Moving to Work agency since 2021, describes Hughes Station as the first stage of its asset management and development strategy for its tax credit properties.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2023 Round One or Round Two applicant reports or the 2023 Round Two award report.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report lists $14,500,000 of bonds, while CHFA's February 2025 newsletter cites $16,340,000 of private activity bonds.
CHFA's award report lists the credit under cycle year 2023, while CHFA's newsletter says the credit was allocated in 2024 and the housing authority says the reservation came in June 2024.
The housing authority's 2024 staff memo gives the address as 233 South Main Street, while CHFA and the authority's other materials give 233 North Main Street.
Within the same memo, the sources table shows $176,000 of county CDBG and a $260,000 Moving to Work loan, while the narrative describes about $350,000 of CDBG and a $370,000 Moving to Work loan.
